question: Is the haze bad in Singapore today?
name: Claude
answer:
Yes, the haze is bad today (17 Oct). Air quality is "unhealthy" in every part of Singapore.

**Readings as of 2pm (The Star / NEA data)**
- **24-hour PSI:** central 184, north 135, south 154, east 173, west 185. Anything from 101 to 200 counts as "unhealthy."
- **Hourly PM2.5, which shows what the air is like right now:** west 243, central 179, south 162, east 159. All four are in the "high" band (151–250). The north is lower at 91, which is "elevated."
- PM2.5 levels went up through the morning, so the air was getting worse as the day went on.

**Background**
- Yesterday the central region hit "very unhealthy," peaking at a PSI of 229, the highest so far this season. Today is a slight improvement on that.
- NEA's forecast for today was a PSI of 150–230. That means it could go back into "very unhealthy" territory.
- Today is the 13th day in a row of unhealthy air since 5 Oct. That's the longest stretch since the 2015 haze crisis.

**NEA's health advice for these levels**
- Everyone should cut down on strenuous outdoor activity.
- Older people, pregnant women, children and anyone with heart or lung disease should avoid it altogether.
- It's a good idea to keep windows closed and use an air purifier if you have one.

Readings change every hour, so check the NEA haze site or myENV app for the latest numbers before you go out.

# Haze in Singapore: PSI back to ‘unhealthy’ range in all regions; PM2.5 enters ‘high’ range in the west
SINGAPORE – The hazy conditions continued in the morning of Oct 17 even as the 24-hour PSI in central Singapore dipped back to the "unhealthy" band after staying in the "very unhealthy" range the day before.

At 11am, the 24-hour PSI was in the "unhealthy" range in all regions: central (184), north (139), south (154), east (174), west (176).

Meanwhile, the hourly PM2.5 readings – measured in micrograms per cubic metre and used as a gauge for current air quality – entered the "high" range in the west at 158 at 11am, while the rest of the island stayed in the "elevated" range, ranging from 83 and 144.



The central region was worst hit on Oct 16 when the 24-hour PSI there registered "very unhealthy" readings throughout the day, peaking at a season high of 229 from 3pm to 4pm, till the early hours of Oct 17.

Singapore air quality enters very unhealthy range
The Singapore haze as seen in Sengkang at 6.45am on Oct 24, 2015. u00e2u20acu201d TODAY pic

SINGAPORE, Oct 24 — Hazy conditions on the island worsened this morning. Air quality entered the very healthy range at 4am, and the 24-hour PSI had climbed since.

At 11am, the 24-hour PSI is in the 186-229 range. The three-hour PSI is at 178, down from 1am’s 232.

Yesterday, the National Environment Agency (NEA) said the hazy conditions are expected to continue today, with the 24-hour Pollutant Standards Index (PSI) for the next 24 hours is expected to be in the mid to high sections of the unhealthy range over the next 24 hours, and may enter the low end of the very unhealthy range if denser haze is blown in.

Reduced visibility is also expected to persist.

The NEA said that some haze from Kalimantan had spread to the surrounding region, and was being blown in by the prevailing south-easterly winds.

SINGAPORE, Sept 15 — The current hazy condition persists in Singapore, with the air quality continuing to stay at an unhealthy level.

The National Environment Agency (NEA) said today, the prevailing winds are forecast to blow from the southwest, and the current hazy conditions are expected to persist.

As of 8am today, the 24-hour pollutant standard index (PSI) stood at 122 - 150, and the three-hour PSI at 114.

A 24-hour PSI reading of above 100 indicates unhealthy air quality.

The haze situation could further deteriorate should the current unfavourable winds blow in denser haze from Sumatra.

Thundery showers are forecast for Singapore in early morning hours, but this may only bring a brief temporary respite to the hazy conditions. — Bernama
